questions.question: Explain two reasons why Clemenceau wanted a harsh treaty. (4 marks)

points.text: France had suffered the most in WWI: 1.3 million dead and northern France devastated by German occupation and fighting. Clemenceau feared future German attacks and wanted to permanently weaken Germany so it could never invade again. He also wanted to recover Alsace-Lorraine (lost in 1871) and gain massive reparations to rebuild France's destroyed regions.

questions.question: How far were the Big Three satisfied with the Treaty of Versailles? (8 marks)

points.text: Clemenceau was partially satisfied: he gained Alsace-Lorraine, reparations, and military restrictions on Germany. However, he wanted even harsher terms - an independent Rhineland and the permanent breakup of Germany. questions.question: "The Treaty of Versailles made another war inevitable." How far do you agree? (16 marks)

points.text: The Treaty made another war more likely but not inevitable. It created the conditions for future conflict: German resentment fuelled revisionism; the "stab-in-the-back" myth undermined the Weimar Republic; economic hardship from reparations destabilised German democracy; the Polish Corridor and Sudetenland created ongoing disputes.
